home.metaTitle: British Footprints: Istanbul – self-guided history walks and map app
home.metaDesc: 51 places and 7 self-guided walks that trace British history in Istanbul: Crimean War Scutari, the embassies of Pera, Victorian engravings then and now. Offline pictures, English and Turkish, for iPhone and Android.
home.ogDesc: A self-guided history map of British Istanbul: 51 places, 7 walks, Victorian engravings then and now.
home.heroAlt: A Victorian engraving of the Bosphorus and the old city of Istanbul with app map pins and a dotted walking route
home.eyebrow: iPhone and Android · English and Turkish
home.h1: The British footprints of Istanbul, on foot
home.lead: A map and pocket guide to 51 places where British travellers, soldiers, diplomats, architects and artists left their mark on Istanbul – from the Crimean War barracks at Scutari to the embassies of Pera. Pick a place, read its story, and walk there.
home.insideLead: Every place sits on the map, grouped by theme. Tap it for the story, the pictures and a short note on visiting.
home.appAlt: Two phones: the British Footprints map of Istanbul with themed pins, and a place page showing a Victorian engraving of Seraglio Point
home.f1Body: Embassies and consulates, Crimean War barracks and cemeteries, Anglican churches, British-built banks, schools and railways, writers' haunts and film locations – each with a story, its period, its district and visiting notes.
home.f2Body: From the Asian shore at Üsküdar through British Pera, along the Bosphorus by ferry, to Kadıköy and Moda and the old city in Victorian engravings. Each walk is a route of numbered stops.
home.f3Body: See Istanbul as Bartlett, Allom and other Victorian artists drew it, then stand on the same spot today. Historic and modern pictures, all freely licensed and credited.
home.f4Body: The stories and all the pictures are inside the app, so they work without mobile data. Only the street map loads over the internet.
home.f5Title: Directions in Apple Maps or Google Maps
home.f5Body: Tap Directions to walk to a place, or hand a whole walk to your maps app with one button.
home.f6Title: Your location stays on your phone
home.f6Body: Distances and the “you are here” dot are worked out on the phone. No account, no ads, no tracking.
home.freeLead: Download the app for free and explore before you decide.
home.free1: The full map with all 51 places
home.free2: A first look at every place: its first picture, the facts and the opening of its story
home.free3: The complete Üsküdar walk – Scutari in the Crimean War: 4 stops with full stories and directions
home.unlock2: All 7 walks, handed to your maps app
home.unlockNote: One purchase – no subscription and no ads. The App Store or Google Play shows the price in your currency.

home.s2: The British Pera walk with its numbered stops
home.s3: Explore by theme – free places are marked
home.s4: Locked places show the opening of their story

home.faq1q: Is this a self-guided walking tour of Istanbul?
home.faq1a: Yes. The seven walks are self-guided routes with numbered stops and a story at each one. You walk at your own pace, and the app hands the stops to Apple Maps or Google Maps for walking directions.
home.faq2q: Which places are in the app?
home.faq2a: 51 places linked to British history in Istanbul, for example Selimiye Barracks and the Haidar Pasha British war cemetery at Scutari, Pera House and the summer embassy at Tarabya, the Crimean Memorial Church, the Ottoman Bank in Galata, the Tünel railway, the British village of Moda in Kadıköy and the viewpoints of the Victorian engravers.
home.faq3a: The stories and all the pictures are inside the app and work without a connection. The street map comes from OpenStreetMap and needs mobile data or Wi-Fi.
home.faq4q: What is free, and what does the unlock include?
home.faq4a: The map, a first look at every place and the whole Üsküdar walk are free. One purchase unlocks all 51 stories, all 7 walks, every picture, directions to every place and future content updates.
home.faq5a: No. It is a one-time purchase with no ads. On another phone or after reinstalling, use “Restore purchases” with the same Apple ID or Google account.
home.faq6a: English and Turkish. You can switch the language in the app's settings.
home.faq7q: Do I need to be in Istanbul to use it?
home.faq7a: No. You can read the stories and plan your walks at home. Distances and the “you are here” dot appear once you are in the city and allow location access.
home.faq8a: No. There is no account, no advertising and no tracking. The app sends anonymous usage statistics that you can switch off in Settings; the privacy policy lists exactly what they contain.
home.ctaLead: 51 places, 7 walks, one map – free to try.
privacy.metaDesc: How the British Footprints: Istanbul app handles location, anonymous usage statistics, purchases and maps. No account, no ads, no tracking.
privacy.lead: British Footprints: Istanbul is built to need as little data as possible. There is no account, no advertising and no tracking. This page explains, in plain words, everything the app and this website do with data.
privacy.sum1: Your location is used on your phone. Your coordinates are never stored or sent; the statistics only say whether the phone is in Istanbul (approximate location).
privacy.sum2: Anonymous usage statistics go to TelemetryDeck (Germany). No name, no e-mail, no search text, no coordinates. You can switch them off.
privacy.sum3: Purchases are handled by Apple or Google. We never see your payment details.
privacy.sum4: No account, no ads, no cookies, no tracking across apps or websites.
privacy.factWhoV: Mehmet Gökhan Memik, trading as thebarnapp (sole proprietorship), Istanbul, Türkiye
privacy.whoBody: The app is published by thebarnapp, the sole proprietorship of Mehmet Gökhan Memik in Istanbul, Türkiye. He is responsible for the data processing described here. For any question or request, write to app@save-all.com.
privacy.locBody: If you allow location access, the app uses your position only on your phone: to show the “you are here” dot on the map and to measure the distance to each place. Your coordinates are never stored and never sent to us or to anyone else.
privacy.locBody2: The only thing derived from your location that leaves the phone is a yes/no/unknown value in the usage statistics (section 3): whether the phone is within about 30 km of central Istanbul. In the App Store and Google Play privacy details this is listed as approximate location, used for analytics only, not linked to you and not used for tracking. The app works fully without location access; you can allow or withdraw it at any time in your phone's settings.
privacy.anaBody: To learn which places and features are used, the app sends anonymous usage statistics to TelemetryDeck GmbH, a privacy-focused analytics service based in Germany (EU). The statistics are short signals such as “a place page was opened” or “a walk was started in Maps”. They contain no name, no e-mail address, no search text and no location coordinates.
privacy.anaWhat1: Screens and features: app start (first start or not), which screen or tab is shown (map, explore, walks, settings, place, walk, preview, unlock screen, credits, privacy).
privacy.anaWhat2: Places and walks: which place or walk was opened, previewed, marked as visited or favourite, or handed to a maps app – identified by the app's own content id (for example “pera-house”), its theme, and whether it is free or locked; for directions, which maps app was used (Apple Maps, Google Maps, the system choice or the browser).
privacy.anaWhat3: Map and search: theme filters and the favourites filter on the map or list, the “Free: start here” hint (shown, tapped, retired), and for searches only the number of results and the length of the query in buckets (such as 3–5 letters) – never the search text.
privacy.anaWhat4: Unlock and purchases: the unlock screen shown or closed and what opened it, a purchase started, completed, cancelled, pending or failed (with a general reason), restore requested and its result, a redeem code sheet opened, and whether a completed purchase was a real one, a store test or a promo code. For a real purchase the unlock’s fixed list price in US dollars (0.99) is counted so we can see sales; never your local price, store country or payment data.
privacy.anaWhat5: Settings: theme, language and maps app changed, marks cleared, and the statistics switch itself (switching off sends one last signal, then nothing more).
privacy.anaWhat6: Location availability: once per session, if location cannot be used, the general reason (location services off, permission denied, or unknown).
privacy.ctxChannel: How the app was installed: development, TestFlight, App Store, Google Play, internal or closed test, or unknown.
privacy.ctxEntitled: Whether the one-time unlock has been bought (yes/no).
privacy.ctxLang: The app's language: English, Turkish or other.
privacy.ctxTheme: The app's theme: dark, light or phone setting.
privacy.ctxIst: Whether the phone is within about 30 km of central Istanbul: yes, no or unknown. Worked out on the phone; the coordinates never leave it.
privacy.anaSdk: The TelemetryDeck software adds technical details such as the app version and build number, the operating system and its version, the device model and the phone's language and region settings, and starts a session signal when the app opens (on Android also a signal when a new installation is detected).
privacy.anaId: To count users rather than app starts, the app creates a random identifier. It is hashed with a salt on the phone before it is sent, so TelemetryDeck receives a value that cannot be traced back to you, your device or your store account. It is not linked to any other data about you and is not used for advertising or tracking across apps or websites. TelemetryDeck receives the data over an encrypted connection; like any internet server it sees the connection's IP address, and it states that it does not store it.
privacy.anaTest: Builds for testing (development builds, TestFlight and closed Android tests) send their statistics marked as test data, kept apart from the statistics of the published app from the App Store and Google Play.
privacy.anaOpt: Open the app's Settings and switch off “Share anonymous usage statistics”. The app then sends one last signal saying that statistics were switched off, stops the analytics software and sends nothing more. The choice is saved on the phone; while it is off, the analytics software is not started at all.
privacy.anaBasis: Legal basis: our legitimate interest in understanding, in anonymous form, how the guide is used so that we can improve it (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR), with the right to object at any time through the switch above.
privacy.buyBody: The one-time unlock is sold and paid through the Apple App Store or Google Play, under Apple's or Google's own terms and privacy policies. We never see your name, payment details or store account. The app only receives the store's confirmation that the unlock was bought and remembers it on your phone.
privacy.mapBody: The street map is made of map tiles loaded from OpenStreetMap's servers. Like any website, those servers see your IP address and the requested map area when they deliver a tile. Their handling is described in the OpenStreetMap Foundation privacy policy.
privacy.picBody: All pictures and stories are bundled inside the app. Viewing them sends no request anywhere.
privacy.handTitle: 7. Directions in Apple Maps or Google Maps
privacy.handBody: When you tap Directions or start a walk in Maps, the app opens Apple Maps, Google Maps or another maps app (or a web browser) and passes it the destination – the place or the stops of the walk. From then on, that app handles the route under its own privacy policy.
privacy.deviceBody: Your language and theme, the maps app you chose, the places you mark as visited or favourite, the statistics switch and the record that you bought the unlock are saved only on your phone. Use “Clear” in the settings or delete the app to remove them.
privacy.noTitle: 9. No accounts, no ads, no tracking
privacy.noBody: There is no sign-in and no advertising. The app does not ask for your name or e-mail, does not use the advertising identifier and does not track you across other apps or websites. We do not sell or share data.
privacy.webBody: This website uses no cookies, no analytics and no third-party scripts; its fonts are served from the site itself. Your language and theme choice are saved in your browser's local storage and never sent. The site is hosted on GitHub Pages; GitHub processes server logs, including IP addresses, as described in the GitHub privacy statement.
privacy.kidsBody: The app is a history guide for a general audience and is not directed at children. It collects no personal data from anyone, children included.
privacy.rightsBody: Depending on where you live (for example under the GDPR, the UK GDPR or Turkey's KVKK), you have the right to access, correct or delete personal data, to restrict or object to processing and to complain to a data protection authority. Because the statistics are anonymous, we cannot link them to you, but you can always switch them off. Write to app@save-all.com with any request.
privacy.srcBody: The pictures come from Wikimedia Commons and are in the public domain (including CC0) or under Creative Commons licences (CC BY and CC BY-SA, versions 2.0 to 4.0). Every picture shows its author, source and licence under the image, and the full list is in the app under Settings › Credits & licences. Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors, available under the Open Database License (ODbL). Fonts: Playfair Display and Lora, SIL Open Font License 1.1.
privacy.changeBody: If the app's handling of data changes, this page will be updated before the new version is released, and the effective date below will change.
support.metaDesc: Help with British Footprints: Istanbul: restoring the unlock, offline use, location permission, directions in Apple Maps and Google Maps, language, theme and contact.
support.lead: Something not working, or a question about a place? Write to us – every message is read and answered.
support.mailHint: Please mention your phone model, its system version and the app version (Settings › About).
support.faq1q: How do I restore my purchase on a new phone or after reinstalling?
support.faq1a: Open Settings › Full access › Restore purchases (the button is also on the unlock screen). Use the same Apple ID or Google account you bought with. The app also checks quietly at start, so a reinstalled app usually unlocks by itself once it is online. On iPhone you can enter a promotional code with Redeem code.
support.faq2q: Can my family use the unlock?
support.faq2a: Yes on iPhone and iPad: the unlock supports Family Sharing, so up to five family members in your Apple family group get it too (open the app and tap Restore purchases). On Android the unlock belongs to the Google account that bought it and works on every device signed in with that account; Google Play does not share in-app purchases with a family group.
support.faq3q: Does the app work without mobile data?
support.faq3a: Yes for the stories and pictures: they are inside the app. The street map is loaded from OpenStreetMap and needs a connection; without one, the places and walks are still listed and readable.
support.faq4q: Why does the app ask for my location, and can I say no?
support.faq4a: Your location is used only on your phone, to show the “you are here” dot and the distance to each place. It is never stored or sent. You can say no – everything else works. To change it later: on iPhone, Settings › Privacy & Security › Location Services › British Footprints; on Android, Settings › Apps › British Footprints › Permissions › Location.
support.faq5q: How do directions work in Apple Maps and Google Maps?
support.faq5a: On a place page, tap Directions for walking directions to it. On a walk, tap Start the walk in Maps. Google Maps takes the whole walk with all its stops. Apple Maps gives walking directions to one stop at a time: mark the stop as visited and tap again for the next one. On iPhone the app asks once which maps app to use; you can change it in Settings. On Android, Google Maps is used for whole walks.
support.faq6q: How do I turn off the usage statistics?
support.faq6a: Open Settings and switch off Share anonymous usage statistics. The statistics are anonymous anyway – the privacy policy lists exactly what they contain.
support.faq7q: How do I change the language or the dark/light theme?
support.faq7a: In Settings, choose English or Turkish under Language, and Dark, Light or “Use phone setting” under Appearance. Stories without a translation are shown in English.
support.faq8q: I found a mistake in a story. How do I report it?
support.faq8a: Thank you! Please write to app@save-all.com with the name of the place, what is wrong and, if you can, a source. Every story lists its sources in the app, and corrections are included in the next update.
support.faq9q: I bought the unlock, but places are still locked.
support.faq9a: Make sure the phone is online and signed in to the store account you bought with, then tap Restore purchases in Settings › Full access. If a payment is still pending (for example Ask to Buy), the unlock arrives once it is approved. If it still does not work, write to us.
